assessment.nobel_worthiness: The framework of nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and interest-rate rules is the working core of modern monetary policy analysis and practice in central banks. The contributions are conceptually foundational and have been tested for decades.
assessment.attribution: The pool is wide (eight names). A three-person core is defensible: Calvo for time-dependent price setting, Taylor for staggered contracts and the policy rule, Woodford for the integrated microfounded theory of monetary policy. Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler are close behind, and the cut is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. The key papers date from the 1980s to the early 2000s and their practical influence is well established. The 2011 prize and later prizes touched adjacent macro themes but not this core.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer a different trio, for example one including Christiano and Eichenbaum for empirical DSGE work.
Overlap with earlier macro prizes (Lucas, Sargent-Sims, Kydland-Prescott) may count against it.
I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not verified independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints that amplify and propagate shocks are a central mechanism in macro-finance and the financial-crisis literature. Kiyotaki and Moore's credit-cycle model is one of the most influential macro papers of the past three decades.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is a clear two-person core. Gertler and Gilchrist belong to the financial-accelerator and empirical strand. Bernanke's earlier award in 2022 partly covers that strand, which makes a narrower core natural.
assessment.maturity: Mature. The model dates from 1997 and has had a long period of confirmation and extension, including through the 2008 crisis and in current quantitative macro-finance.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises, which could reduce the marginal appeal.
Whether Gertler should be added as a third laureate for the integration with business-cycle models.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed what is known about intergenerational mobility, its geography and the causal effect of neighbourhoods. The work is empirically transformative and policy-relevant, and it links to the older theory of mobility and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure. Hendren and Friedman are closely tied through the Opportunity Insights projects and the causal-neighbourhood work. Katz is credited for earlier Moving to Opportunity work. Credit is therefore concentrated but the group is large, and I cut it to three.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The core results are from about 2014 to 2022. Replication and follow-up are extensive, but some policy conclusions are still debated.
uncertainties: Very large team science makes credit allocation difficult.
The committee may want more time for long-run confirmation.
Chetty also appears in the optimal-taxation candidate, which complicates the case for a single award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their intertemporal approach to the open economy underlies modern international macroeconomics, including current-account analysis, exchange-rate dynamics and the disconnect puzzles. The textbook and the research programme shaped both the field and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: A clean two-person attribution: the joint 1996 treatise, the 1995 redux model and the exchange-rate puzzle papers. Rogoff also appears in the crisis-history candidate.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature. The core work is from the 1980s to the 1990s and has endured.
uncertainties: Parts of the contribution are synthesis and agenda-setting rather than a single discovery.
Some empirical puzzles remain unresolved, which weakens the claim of settled results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: They provided the dominant political-economy models of trade protection (Protection for Sale), the endogenous-growth and trade framework (Innovation and Growth in the Global Economy), and the foundations of interest-group politics in trade policy. Their influence runs across trade, growth and political economy.
assessment.attribution: A natural pair with longstanding joint authorship. Helpman also appears in the firm-heterogeneity candidate, which supports a broader Helpman case.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with work from the 1980s to the 1990s and decades of applications.
uncertainties: The 2008 trade prize and the recent growth prize reduce the room for another trade or growth award.
Empirical tests of the protection model are mixed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrate household heterogeneity and incomplete markets with nominal rigidities. They changed how monetary and fiscal transmission is analyzed, notably the importance of hand-to-mouth households and indirect effects. The method links to quantitative dynamic general-equilibrium modelling.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll and Violante are the clear authors of the central 2018 paper. They build on earlier heterogeneous-agent work (Aiyagari, Bewley, Huggett, Krusell-Smith) not credited here, which complicates the allocation.
assessment.maturity: Moderate. The core is under ten years old and the framework is still developing. It is widely adopted in central bank research, but not yet fully settled.
uncertainties: Early for a Nobel and the committee may wait.
Predecessor credit and the debate over how much HANK changes policy conclusions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: They reshaped the measurement of long-run top income and wealth distributions and shifted public and academic debate on inequality. The empirical contribution is large, particularly the construction of distributional national accounts and series based on tax data.
assessment.attribution: The three have overlapping, partly joint programmes: Piketty-Saez on top incomes, Saez-Zucman on wealth, and Zucman on offshore wealth. Credit is reasonably clear, though others (Atkinson, who is deceased) matter.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. The top-income work dates from the early 2000s. Parts of the wealth and offshore estimates are still contested.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes about wealth estimates and data construction.
The theoretical content of the explanations (r > g) is more contested than the measurement.
Politically salient work; the committee must separate measurement merit from policy advocacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of resource misallocation across firms and its consequences for cross-country income and TFP differences is a widely used quantitative framework in growth and development. It provided a disciplined way to link micro distortions to aggregate productivity.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the core. Restuccia and Rogerson (not credited here) and Restuccia are closely related. The two-person attribution is defensible, but others could reasonably be included.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature, with about 17 years of application and extension. Critiques concern measurement error and model dependence.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of measured misallocation to measurement error and functional-form assumptions.
The recent growth prize may weigh against another growth-related award soon.
Credit allocation relative to Restuccia and Rogerson.
